## 7. Staging, single publication commit, and terminal-event ordering (addresses F1)

### 7.1 Single publication commit point
The run directory is the unit of atomic publication on the same filesystem:
```
STAGING dir: <results>/_staging/<run_id>/         # not visible as a successful run
  reports/complete_report.md  (and .html if enabled)   # final envelope + checked body
  manifest.json                                        # fully populated incl. terminal_event.durable
COMMIT:  os.replace/rename  <results>/_staging/<run_id>  ->  <results>/<ticker>/<run_id>/
```
- **One commit point.** Everything the manifest describes (report MD/HTML, manifest itself) is written into the **staging** directory **first**; the **only** publication action is a single atomic directory rename. Before the rename, nothing exists at the published path; after it, a complete, self-consistent run directory exists.
- **No success is visible before the commit.** There is no earlier `rename` of the report into the published location; the "report staged but unpublished" state is real because the report lives only under `_staging`.
- **Terminal event ordering (truthful durability):** the **logical** terminal decision is computed before commit. The **JSONL terminal event is appended to the staging `events.jsonl` before the commit**, so its success/failure is **known before** the manifest is finalized. `terminal_event.durable = (jsonl terminal append succeeded)`. A later event append is **not** part of the immutable manifest's claim; best-effort events written after commit are separate and cannot change `manifest.json`.
- **Reader behaviour:** a run directory is a valid published run iff it exists at `<results>/<ticker>/<run_id>/` (the rename completed). `_staging/**` is never treated as a published run. Readers may ignore `_staging`.

### 7.2 Sink criticality
| Sink | Criticality | Rule (with single-commit) |
|---|---|---|
| Report MD (and HTML if enabled) | **Critical** | Written to staging; part of the commit unit |
| Manifest | **Critical** | Written to staging with final `terminal_event.durable`; part of the commit unit |
| JSONL terminal event | **Critical for the `durable` flag** | Appended to staging **before** commit; its outcome sets `terminal_event.durable` |
| Other JSONL progress events | Best-effort | May be appended pre- or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; never changes the immutable manifest |
| State JSON / message log | Best-effort | Written to staging or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; does not flip a completed decision |

### 7.3 Failure mapping (one per path)
- **Critical staging write fails** (report or manifest or terminal-event-to-staging) **before commit:** no rename performed; nothing appears at the published path; result `INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`. Staging dir is cleaned or left under `_staging` (not published).
- **Commit rename fails:** same as above — nothing published; typed `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`.
- **Best-effort sink fails (progress event / state log / message log):** the commit still proceeds; outcome is unchanged (`COMPLETED`/…); a redacted note is recorded; `terminal_event.durable` reflects the **terminal** append only.
- **Logical outcome revision:** `OutcomeFinalizer` produces the logical outcome; only a **critical staging/commit** failure (before any publication) revises the returned result to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`. Since nothing is published before commit, no published PASSED/COMPLETED can contradict the returned result.
- **Full-disk/power-loss durability:** out of scope; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.

### 7.4 Reconciliation with earlier finalization
`OutcomeFinalizer` sends the logical outcome and `terminal_event.durable` into the staging manifest **before** commit. If critical persistence fails, the **returned** result is revised to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` (satisfying INV-08); nothing was published, so there is no stale success artifact.

### 7.5 Chronological failure walkthroughs (document examples; states verified against §7.1–§7.4)
Legend: `VISIBLE` = present at published path; `STAGED` = under `_staging` only.

- **(a) Report staging write fails:** after staging the manifest is attempted? **No** — report write fails first → abort; no manifest, no commit. `STAGED`: partial report maybe; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, rating null, NOT_RUN, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`.
- **(b) Manifest staging write fails:** report written to staging; manifest write fails → abort before commit; `STAGED`: report; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. No published COMPLETED exists.
- **(c) Final publication (rename) fails:** staging complete (report+manifest+terminal event); rename fails → `STAGED`: full run; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. Reader sees no published run.
- **(d) Best-effort JSONL progress write fails (after terminal already staged):** commit proceeds; `VISIBLE`: full run with `manifest.terminal_event.durable=true` (terminal append succeeded); returned `COMPLETED/…`; a redacted note about the dropped progress event. Immutable manifest unchanged by the dropped progress event.
- **(e) Terminal-event append to staging fails:** `terminal_event.durable=false` recorded in the staging manifest; commit still publishes the run directory (report+manifest valid); returned outcome is the logical outcome (COMPLETED if graph returned); a redacted note. The manifest truthfully states the terminal event is **not durable**; no later append alters it.

No walkthrough publishes a report that contradicts the returned terminal result.

## 7. Staging, persistence, publication and terminal-event ordering (addresses B3-05)

### 7.1 Sink criticality
| Sink | Criticality | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Report (MD, and HTML if enabled) | **Critical** | Must stage successfully before publication |
| Manifest | **Critical** | Atomic write-once; commit gates publication success |
| State JSON / message log | Best-effort | Failure ⇒ redacted note; does not flip a completed decision to persistence failure **unless** it is the only artifact the run promises (it is not) |
| JSONL events | Best-effort | Terminal event logical decision always emitted to result; durability qualified (§7.4) |

### 7.2 Ordering
```
finalize → write artifacts to STAGING run dir (not visible as success)
        → atomic publish (rename staging → per-run output location)
        → write manifest last (atomic, write-once)
        → emit terminal event
        → return RunResult
```
- **No successful report is exposed before critical persistence succeeds.** Staging is written under a non-public temp path; publication is an atomic rename; the manifest is written after report publication and before returning success.
- **One failure mapping:** a critical staging/commit failure ⇒ `run_outcome=INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `manifest_path=null`, `report_path=null` (or partial path if a labelled partial was intentionally retained). The returned `RunResult` and any retained artifact agree; no earlier COMPLETED/PASSED is returned.
- **Partial artifacts:** if the graph completed but persistence failed, retained partials are written with an explicit INCOMPLETE label; they are not presented as a successful report.

### 7.3 Reconciliation with earlier finalization
`OutcomeFinalizer` produces the **logical** outcome before persistence; if persistence is critical and fails, the **logical outcome is revised** to INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR for the **returned result and terminal event**, satisfying INV-08 (INCOMPLETE ⇒ no rating, NOT_RUN). A COMPLETED rating is therefore never returned alongside a persistence failure.

### 7.4 Terminal-event guarantee (qualified)
- Exactly **one logical** `run.terminal` decision per run; its content is also carried in `RunResult`.
- If the JSONL sink write fails, the run may still return its (redacted) logical result; manifest records `terminal_event_durable=false`. This preserves a single logical terminal decision while honestly qualifying durability.
- Full-disk/power-loss durability is **out of scope**; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.

### 7.5 Failure simulations (design; document examples)
- **Report staging fails:** nothing published; `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, no manifest, `report_path=null`.
- **State-log write fails:** best-effort note; report+manifest still published; outcome unchanged (COMPLETED/…).
- **Manifest commit fails:** report staged but **not published**; `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no manifest/report path returned.
- **Terminal-event write fails:** logical result returned; `terminal_event_durable=false`; report/manifest may be published (critical path succeeded).

+- **(a) Report staging write fails:** after staging the manifest is attempted? **No** — report write fails first → abort; no manifest, no commit. `STAGED`: partial report maybe; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, rating null, NOT_RUN, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`.
+- **(b) Manifest staging write fails:** report written to staging; manifest write fails → abort before commit; `STAGED`: report; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. No published COMPLETED exists.
+- **(c) Final publication (rename) fails:** staging complete (report+manifest+terminal event); rename fails → `STAGED`: full run; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. Reader sees no published run.
+- **(d) Best-effort JSONL progress write fails (after terminal already staged):** commit proceeds; `VISIBLE`: full run with `manifest.terminal_event.durable=true` (terminal append succeeded); returned `COMPLETED/…`; a redacted note about the dropped progress event. Immutable manifest unchanged by the dropped progress event.
+- **(e) Terminal-event append to staging fails:** `terminal_event.durable=false` recorded in the staging manifest; commit still publishes the run directory (report+manifest valid); returned outcome is the logical outcome (COMPLETED if graph returned); a redacted note. The manifest truthfully states the terminal event is **not durable**; no later append alters it.
+
+No walkthrough publishes a report that contradicts the returned terminal result.
+

- **Estimator:** token counts approximated by `ceil(len(prompt_chars)/4)` (cheap, provider-agnostic; **explicitly estimated**, no guarantee against provider tokenizer; no tokenizer dependency added).
- **Per-agent context cap** `C_cap = 24,000` estimated tokens (proposed): bounds the **assembled prompt context** for one agent, not an aggregate run budget.
- **Critical reserve** `R_reserve = 4,000` estimated tokens (proposed) planned for identity + standing constraints + state/authority + frozen notice/disclaimer; never compacted.
- **Compaction threshold** `T_compact = floor(0.8 · C_cap) = floor(19,200) = 19,200`; compact when estimated context exceeds `T_compact`; hard stop at `C_cap`. (Arithmetic corrected: 0.8 × 24,000 = **19,200**, not 20,000.)
- **Protected-context overflow (actual estimate, not the constant):** let `P` be the **measured estimate of the protected layers** (identity + constraints + state/authority + notice/disclaimer) at assembly time. If `P + (minimum irreducible task/history context) > C_cap`, or more simply if `P > C_cap − C_min_task` (where `C_min_task` is the minimum needed for the current task), **fail closed** (typed `INTERNAL_ERROR`, redacted). The guard compares the **actual protected estimate `P`**, never merely `R_reserve` (which by construction is ≤ `C_cap` and could never overflow).
- **Compaction termination:** compaction reduces only low-priority narrative (debate prose, redundant analyst text) until total ≤ `T_compact` or until the only remaining reducible content is protected; if compacting all reducible narrative still leaves total > `C_cap`, **fail closed**. Available narrative budget = `C_cap − P`; stop when narrative reaches that bound.
- **Compaction method:** summarize/trim **low-priority narrative layers only**; deterministic truncation with an explicit "(compacted)" marker is the baseline. If a summarizing **model call** is used it is an **explicitly disclosed extra provider call** logged as `event=context.compact` — not silent network behaviour. Default design = deterministic truncation (no extra model; consistent with the note that these corrections imply **no new summarizing provider call**).
- **Re-injection:** after compaction re-inject identity, mode, snapshot identity (fingerprint/basename/as-of), output authority and frozen disclaimer/notice.
- **Where:** node-prompt assembly in the agent context layer (`tradingagents/agents/context.py` + prompt builders); **not** OpenCode's internal context.
- **Temporal guards:** memory/context retrieval keeps upstream as-of/time guards; compaction must not reintroduce out-of-window history.

state.output:
**Problem fixed:** the check must run on content that does *not* yet contain its own result, yet the delivered header must display the check result. Resolution: separate the **immutable checked body** from the **trusted final envelope**.

### 6.1 Two-part document
- **Body** (model-generated sections + trusted frozen notice/disclaimer): rendered once from `final_state` + `RunContext`, **redacted before check**.
- **Pre-check provenance fragment** (trusted, deterministic): the exact header lines Q2 will inspect — analysis date, input mode, basename, full-64 fingerprint, as-of/basis — rendered from `SafeInputMetadata` **before** the check. This is the object Q2 compares; it is not the checker comparing metadata to itself, because it is an independently produced text fragment.
- **Envelope** (trusted): the final delivered header, built **after** the check from `SafeRunMetadata` (which now includes outcome/check). It must byte-match the pre-check provenance fragment for its Q2 fields (verified again before publication, §6.4).

### 6.2 Single authoritative check — completed path only (F4)
```
1. final_state  (or an exception → go to 6.3 INCOMPLETE branch; checker NOT called)
2. body = render_body(final_state, RunContext)                 # trusted strings inserted
3. body = redactor.scrub(body)                                 # redaction BEFORE check
4. provenance_fragment = render_provenance(SafeInputMetadata)  # trusted header text Q2 inspects
5. final_rating = run_rating(final_state)  |  REVIEW           # deterministic
6. CheckResult = OutputChecker.evaluate(                        # ONE authoritative call
        provenance_fragment: str,      # Q2 subject (independently rendered trusted text)
        final_rating: str,             # Q1 subject
        rendered_body: str)            # Q3/Q4 subject (disclaimer excluded from Q4)
   # if the checker raises → CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[CHECK_ERROR]} (fail closed, single decision)
7. result = OutcomeFinalizer.finalize(graph_returned=True, final_rating, exc=None)  # COMPLETED
8. envelope = build_envelope(SafeRunMetadata(result, CheckResult))   # uses the FROZEN CheckResult; no second verdict
9. verify_envelope_header_matches(provenance_fragment, envelope)     # publication-time guard (§6.4)
10. final_doc_md = envelope + body ; final_doc_html = render_html(envelope, body)
11. stage → single publication commit (§7)
```
- The checker is invoked **exactly once** on the completed path; the envelope consumes the **frozen** `CheckResult`.
- **Q2 has a real subject:** it compares `provenance_fragment` (trusted, pre-check text) against `SafeInputMetadata`. A defect that changes the rendered basename/fingerprint/as-of in the fragment produces a **Q2** finding, not a guaranteed pass.

### 6.3 Incomplete branch — checker bypassed (F4)
```
1. engine raised OR graph did not return a usable final_state
2. result = OutcomeFinalizer.finalize(graph_returned=False, final_rating=None, exc=exc)
3. CheckResult = CheckResult{output_check:"NOT_RUN", findings:[]}   # assigned directly; checker NOT invoked
4. envelope = build_envelope(SafeRunMetadata(result, CheckResult))   # INCOMPLETE, NOT_RUN, no rating
5. no successful report body is published as PASSED; partial artifacts labelled INCOMPLETE (§7)
```
The checker signature never receives graph-returned data on this path, so there is no contradictory double verdict.

### 6.4 Envelope verification and source-of-truth (F4)
- `OutputChecker.evaluate(provenance_fragment, final_rating, rendered_body)` calls no provider. Q1 = rating readable; **Q2 = every Q2-envelope field equals the trusted snapshot** (by comparing the pre-check `provenance_fragment` to `SafeInputMetadata`); Q3 = disclaimer present in body; Q4 = prohibited phrases absent in body (disclaimer excluded).
- **Publication-time guard:** before the commit, the build verifies that the envelope's Q2 fields equal the pre-check `provenance_fragment`; a mismatch aborts publication as `CHECK_ERROR`/NEEDS_REVIEW — the trusted metadata remains authoritative.
- **Single source for the disclaimer:** the disclaimer is rendered **once** into the body from the frozen string; the envelope references its presence (Q3) rather than re-emitting a second copy, avoiding body/envelope duplication mismatch.
- **Redaction precedes checks**, so a checked artifact cannot later be invalidated by redaction.

### 6.5 Walkthroughs (synthetic; document examples; verified against §6.2–§6.4)
- **Completed-PASS (no-portfolio):** `final_rating="Hold"`; `provenance_fragment` renders `input_mode=NO_PORTFOLIO`, basename/fingerprint/as-of `null`; body has disclaimer, no prohibited phrase → `CheckResult{PASSED,[]}`; `RunResult{COMPLETED, stop_reason=null, final_rating="Hold", output_check=PASSED}`; envelope shows PASSED; guard passes.
- **Completed-REVIEW (Q2 defect):** renderer bug emits `basename="c.json"` in `provenance_fragment` vs trusted `b.json` → Q2 broken → `CheckResult{NEEDS_REVIEW,[Q2]}`; `RunResult{COMPLETED, output_check=NEEDS_REVIEW}`; publication guard also catches envelope/trusted mismatch and blocks a clean pass.
- **Completed-REVIEW (Q4):** body contains `guaranteed profit` outside disclaimer → `Finding{Q4}`; `NEEDS_REVIEW`.

`interface-contracts.md` §7.3 (line 454) includes terminal-event-to-staging failure among critical failures that prevent commit and return INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR. Section 7.5(e) (line 470) instead commits the report and manifest with `terminal_event.durable=false`. `runtime-policy-catalog.md` R13a and R14 repeat these conflicting outcomes.

Recommended resolution: reports and manifest are critical; terminal JSONL append is best-effort. Remove terminal append from the critical-failure list, retain the logical outcome on append failure, record durable=false before manifest staging, and align all summaries. If the team chooses a critical terminal event instead, remove the contradictory continuation case everywhere. Either is a design choice; both cannot apply to the same trigger.

### H2 — Delete the stale empty-findings equivalence

`interface-contracts.md` §3.3 line 154 still states `PASSED ⇔ findings==[]`, immediately after a correct table that also assigns empty findings to NOT_RUN. Keep the table and use:

- Completed: PASSED iff findings are empty; NEEDS_REVIEW iff at least one blocking finding.
- Incomplete: NOT_RUN with empty findings; checker not invoked.

The checker signature in `interface-contracts.md` §6 accepts provenance_fragment, final_rating and body, but its Q2 rule also needs the trusted SafeInputMetadata. Supply that explicit argument or define constructor-bound trusted metadata; do not leave it as unspecified ambient state.

- **C:** build the independent test plan and fixture inventory, including H1-H3 negative cases; use synthetic holdings and no-network models. Record test-plan approval before implementation.

Do not treat current Markdown permissions as enforcement.
- **D:** inspect module/interfaces and prepare estimates/implementation plan. Begin affected implementation only after H1-H3 are resolved, A's relevant scope approval and the required test/governance gates. Existing raw engine availability is not permission for product CLI paths to bypass the shared boundary.
- **B:** request a narrow documentation patch, preserve authentic OpenCode interventions, then publish a versioned/revision-identified handoff with resolved decisions and pending external-owner items.

### 7.3 Failure mapping (one per path)
- **Critical staging write fails** (report or manifest or terminal-event-to-staging) **before commit:** no rename performed; nothing appears at the published path; result `INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`. - **Commit rename fails:** same as above — nothing published; typed `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`.
- **Best-effort sink fails (progress event / state log / message log):** the commit still proceeds; outcome is unchanged (`COMPLETED`/…); a redacted note is recorded; `terminal_event.durable` reflects the **terminal** append only.
- **Logical outcome revision:** `OutcomeFinalizer` produces the logical outcome; only a **critical staging/commit** failure (before any publication) revises the returned result to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`. Since nothing is published before commit, no published PASSED/COMPLETED can contradict the returned result.
- **Full-disk/power-loss durability:** out of scope; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.

### 7.4 Reconciliation with earlier finalization
`OutcomeFinalizer` sends the logical outcome and `terminal_event.durable` into the staging manifest **before** commit. If critical persistence fails, the **returned** result is revised to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` (satisfying INV-08); nothing was published, so there is no stale success artifact.

### 7.5 Chronological failure walkthroughs (document examples; states verified against §7.1–§7.4)
Legend: `VISIBLE` = present at published path; `STAGED` = under `_staging` only.

- **(a) Report staging write fails:** after staging the manifest is attempted? **No** — report write fails first → abort; no manifest, no commit. `STAGED`: partial report maybe; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, rating null, NOT_RUN, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`.
- **(b) Manifest staging write fails:** report written to staging; manifest write fails → abort before commit; `STAGED`: report; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. No published COMPLETED exists.
- **(c) Final publication (rename) fails:** staging complete (report+manifest+terminal event); rename fails → `STAGED`: full run; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. Reader sees no published run.
- **(d) Best-effort JSONL progress write fails (after terminal already staged):** commit proceeds; `VISIBLE`: full run with `manifest.terminal_event.durable=true` (terminal append succeeded); returned `COMPLETED/…`; a redacted note about the dropped progress event. Immutable manifest unchanged by the dropped progress event.
- **(e) Terminal-event append to staging fails:** `terminal_event.durable=false` recorded in the staging manifest; commit still publishes the run directory (report+manifest valid); returned outcome is the logical outcome (COMPLETED if graph returned); a redacted note. The manifest truthfully states the terminal event is **not durable**; no later append alters it.

No walkthrough publishes a report that contradicts the returned terminal result.

### 3.3 `CheckResult` (F3 — case table)

CheckResult {

}
```
Authoritative case table (**checker is invoked only on the completed path**, §6):

| Case | `output_check` | `findings` | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| All rules hold | `PASSED` | `[]` (exactly empty) | Completed run; Q1–Q4 all hold |
| Any rule broken OR checker exception | `NEEDS_REVIEW` | **≥ 1** blocking finding (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4, or a single `CHECK_ERROR` on exception) | Completed run |
| Run incomplete | `NOT_RUN` | `[]` (exactly empty) | Checker **not invoked**; assigned by finalizer branch (§6) |

## 7. Staging, single publication commit, and terminal-event ordering (addresses F1)

### 7.1 Single publication commit point
The run directory is the unit of atomic publication on the same filesystem:
```
STAGING dir: <results>/_staging/<run_id>/         # not visible as a successful run

metadata.output:
| Manifest | **Critical** | Written to staging with final `terminal_event.durable`; part of the commit unit |
| JSONL terminal event | **Critical for the `durable` flag** | Appended to staging **before** commit; its outcome sets `terminal_event.durable` |
| Other JSONL progress events | Best-effort | May be appended pre- or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; never changes the immutable manifest |
| State JSON / message log | Best-effort | Written to staging or post-commit; failure ⇒ redacted note; does not flip a completed decision |

### 7.3 Failure mapping (one per path)
- **Critical staging write fails** (report or manifest or terminal-event-to-staging) **before commit:** no rename performed; nothing appears at the published path; result `INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`. Staging dir is cleaned or left under `_staging` (not published).
- **Commit rename fails:** same as above — nothing published; typed `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`.
- **Best-effort sink fails (progress event / state log / message log):** the commit still proceeds; outcome is unchanged (`COMPLETED`/…); a redacted note is recorded; `terminal_event.durable` reflects the **terminal** append only.
- **Logical outcome revision:** `OutcomeFinalizer` produces the logical outcome; only a **critical staging/commit** failure (before any publication) revises the returned result to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`. Since nothing is published before commit, no published PASSED/COMPLETED can contradict the returned result.
- **Full-disk/power-loss durability:** out of scope; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.

### 7.4 Reconciliation with earlier finalization
`OutcomeFinalizer` sends the logical outcome and `terminal_event.durable` into the staging manifest **before** commit. If critical persistence fails, the **returned** result is revised to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR` (satisfying INV-08); nothing was published, so there is no stale success artifact.

### 7.5 Chronological failure walkthroughs (document examples; states verified against §7.1–§7.4)
Legend: `VISIBLE` = present at published path; `STAGED` = under `_staging` only.

- **(a) Report staging write fails:** after staging the manifest is attempted? **No** — report write fails first → abort; no manifest, no commit. `STAGED`: partial report maybe; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, rating null, NOT_RUN, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`.
- **(b) Manifest staging write fails:** report written to staging; manifest write fails → abort before commit; `STAGED`: report; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. No published COMPLETED exists.
- **(c) Final publication (rename) fails:** staging complete (report+manifest+terminal event); rename fails → `STAGED`: full run; `VISIBLE`: nothing; returned `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`; no paths. Reader sees no published run.
- **(d) Best-effort JSONL progress write fails (after terminal already staged):** commit proceeds; `VISIBLE`: full run with `manifest.terminal_event.durable=true` (terminal append succeeded); returned `COMPLETED/…`; a redacted note about the dropped progress event. Immutable manifest unchanged by the dropped progress event.
- **(e) Terminal-event append to staging fails:** `terminal_event.durable=false` recorded in the staging manifest; commit still publishes the run directory (report+manifest valid); returned outcome is the logical outcome (COMPLETED if graph returned); a redacted note. The manifest truthfully states the terminal event is **not durable**; no later append alters it.

No walkthrough publishes a report that contradicts the returned terminal result.

### 7.3 Failure mapping (one per path)
- **Critical staging write fails** (report or manifest) **before commit:** no rename performed; nothing appears at the published path; result `INCOMPLETE`, `stop_reason=PERSISTENCE_ERROR`, `final_rating=null`, `output_check=NOT_RUN`, `findings=[]`, `report_path=null`, `manifest_path=null`. - **Terminal-event append to staging fails (best-effort):** the **logical outcome is preserved** (`COMPLETED` if the graph returned); `terminal_event.durable=false` is recorded in the staging manifest **before** commit; the run directory is still published (report+manifest valid). This is **not** a critical failure and does **not** return `PERSISTENCE_ERROR`.
- **Logical outcome revision:** `OutcomeFinalizer` produces the logical outcome; only a **critical report/manifest staging-or-commit** failure (before any publication) revises the returned result to `INCOMPLETE/PERSISTENCE_ERROR`. Since nothing is published before commit, no published PASSED/COMPLETED can contradict the returned result.
- **Full-disk/power-loss durability:** out of scope; `PERSISTENCE_ERROR` is the cooperative contract.

27: ## Findings
28: 
29: ### F1 — P1: Publication cleanup can delete another run's work, including an out-of-root path
30: 
31: **Owner:** D; C adds regression coverage.
32: 
33: **Locations:** `tradingagents/runapi/persist.py:30–40,83–86`; `tradingagents/runapi/context.py:108–112`.
34: 
35: `publish_run()` refuses a pre-existing staging directory, then its exception handler recursively deletes that same directory. The invocation has not established ownership of it. A repeated run ID or a concurrent call can therefore destroy another run's staged files while claiming to refuse overwrite.
36: 
37: Additionally, the run ID is joined directly into paths and the public context validates only that it is nonempty. A supplied ID such as `../../outside` can make cleanup operate outside the results directory. This was reproduced exclusively inside a fresh temporary directory: a sentinel under an existing `_staging/same-run/` was deleted; a second sentinel under a synthetic directory outside `results/` was also deleted. Normally generated IDs are safe; the defect concerns accepted caller-supplied/reused IDs and cleanup ownership.
38: 
39: **Acceptance:** validate run IDs as single safe path components and enforce resolved containment; clean up only a staging directory created and owned by the current invocation. Add collision, concurrent/reused-ID, traversal, absolute-path, and cleanup-ownership cases. Existing work must survive rejected publication.
40: 
41: ### F2 — P1: Credential-style text can survive the redaction boundary
42: 
43: **Owner:** D; C tests each relevant output/diagnostic sink.
44: 
45: **Location:** `tradingagents/runapi/redact.py:7–12,17–25,40–41`.
46: 
47: The string filter does not redact an environment-style label with a provider prefix. The synthetic string `OPENAI_API_KEY=[REDACTED] is returned unchanged. The word boundary before `api_key` does not match after an underscore. Dictionary key filtering handles this case differently, but free text and exception diagnostics use the string path, which is also used for persisted reports/logs.
48: 
49: This demonstrates a bypass; it does not establish that a real credential has already leaked.
50: 
51: **Acceptance:** cover provider-prefixed labels, quoted/multiline credential assignments, authorization forms, and actual configured secret values using synthetic canaries. Verify persisted artifacts and diagnostics, not only dictionaries. Avoid recording real secrets in fixtures or evidence.
52: 
53: ### F3 — P1: The semantic gate accepts a sparse, unrelated scoring sheet as PASS
54: 
55: **Owner:** C; E must not treat this scorer as a sufficient production gate yet.
56: 
57: **Locations:** `tests/member_c_verification/live/score_gov004.py:113–127,152–167,212–236`.
58: 
59: The scorer sums whatever answer rows are present. It does not verify that case/attempt IDs refer to the selected runs, that every applicable rubric item is present exactly once, or that critical items were evaluated. Artifact eligibility checks file existence without checking the manifest's identity or its correspondence to the report.
60: 
61: A synthetic fixture with ten mechanically eligible completed rows, placeholder reports, empty `{}` manifests, and **one score of 1 for an unrelated case/run** returned exit code 0 and `FINAL VERDICT: PASS`. The documented current rubric requires 28 applicable answers for the ten-run population. The existing exit-code tests check verdict-to-exit-code behavior; they do not establish completeness of the semantic assessment.
62: 
63: **Acceptance:** validate scoring and evidence schemas; bind scores to selected case/run/trial IDs; derive required rubric cells from a frozen applicability matrix; reject missing, duplicate, unknown, and inapplicably N/A cells. Verify manifest identity/configuration/revision and artifact correspondence. Add negative fixtures where these defects prevent PASS. Human judgment of narrative quality remains necessary.
64: 
65: ### F4 — P2: Selecting only completed replacements hides failures from the completion denominator
66: 
67: **Owner:** C, with A confirming the formal population; D retains application-level accounting.
68: 
69: **Locations:** `tests/member_c_verification/live/score_gov004.py:130–148,193–221`; `docs/req/selected-requirements.md:116–120`.
70: 
71: The scorer selects the first two eligible **completed** attempts per case and compares the selected count with a constant ten. Failed starts appear in the printed history but cannot reduce the reported completion fraction when later attempts replace them.
72: 
73: A synthetic population of 20 started runs, ten incomplete and ten completed, still reported `completed runs: 10/10 ... PASS`. SEL-TA-NFR-006 requires all started fresh runs in the completion denominator, which would be 10/20 for that population.
74: 
75: **Acceptance:** report overall started/completed/review-needed/incomplete counts and the true completion fraction separately from semantic scores on completed reports. If the formal gate uses a particular ten-attempt cohort, freeze its membership before outcomes are known, retain its failed slots, and report retries separately. Reconcile that policy explicitly with NFR-006. This probe does not prove the documented latest ten-run live population contained failures; it exposes the scorer's behavior when failures occur.

78: 
79: **Owner:** C.
80: 
81: **Locations:** `tests/member_c_verification/offline/test_nfr005_layering.py:19–25,45–66`.

The observed source-file count is **zero**. An empty offender list therefore does not demonstrate the required dependency direction or absence of terminal prompting in the engine layers.

Cover actual prompt entry points used by this project, including `typer`/direct input as appropriate to the approved rule. Re-run the check before retaining its verification claim.

Its specific error detail and intended retry/cancel interaction are unreachable on that path. Tests of the input service alone do not cover this CLI behavior.

95: **Acceptance:** isolate number parsing from file loading or catch the more specific exception first. Test a valid selection of malformed JSON/invalid fields and verify an actionable file diagnostic and the intended retry/cancel flow, with no engine/provider call.

# Project integration review — 2026-11-18

Reviewed by Codex for Member B. This is a review record, not an implementation, approval, or replacement for Member C's independent verification.

## Checkout and result

- Canonical checkout: `/home/brian/projects/CS5351` (Ubuntu WSL).
- Branch: `main`, fast-forwarded from `d94c9f8` to `ee7a0a8e0179b6876ec7f8c1b434c50d1228023c`, matching `origin/main` at fetch time. The new head merges Member C's pull request #3.
- The existing checkout was clean before the update. Application code, tests, requirements, architecture, and governance files were not changed during this review.
- Review scope: integration changes, shared execution/input/publication boundaries, C's offline tests and live-evaluation harness/scorer, requirements/architecture alignment, and repository delivery readiness.
- Conclusion: useful progress and a green offline baseline, but **not ready for unconditional acceptance or a project-wide compliance claim**. Resolve F1–F7 and F9, and make F8 auditable; A/E deliverables also remain pending.

## Initial validation (before the authorized live follow-up)

An isolated `.venv` was installed in this checkout using `pip install -e ".[dev]"` with Python 3.14. This does not update the separate TradingAgents installation or its shortcut.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `GOV004_LIVE=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --tb=short` | 1,500 passed; 2 skipped; 1 deselected; 100 subtests passed; 24 warnings |
| `.venv/bin/ruff check . --output-format concise --statistics` | Passed |
| `.venv/bin/python -m pip check` | No broken requirements found |
| Default GOV-004 scorer, with no saved live evidence | Reports zero evidence files and **PENDING** |
| Targeted synthetic review probes | Reproduced the staging cleanup, redaction, scorer, denominator, and empty-scan issues below |

The skipped tests include the opt-in live evaluation and optional Bedrock dependency support. The default pytest selection excludes integration-marked tests. The initial review made no live model calls. Subsequently authorized school-API diagnostics are recorded in the follow-up below. The synthetic defect probes used no real holdings or credential values. Passing this suite establishes an offline regression baseline, not correctness of every requirement.

## Findings

### F1 — P1: Publication cleanup can delete another run's work, including an out-of-root path

**Owner:** D; C adds regression coverage.

**Locations:** `tradingagents/runapi/persist.py:30–40,83–86`; `tradingagents/runapi/context.py:108–112`.

`publish_run()` refuses a pre-existing staging directory, then its exception handler recursively deletes that same directory. The invocation has not established ownership of it. A repeated run ID or a concurrent call can therefore destroy another run's staged files while claiming to refuse overwrite.

Additionally, the run ID is joined directly into paths and the public context validates only that it is nonempty. A supplied ID such as `../../outside` can make cleanup operate outside the results directory. This was reproduced exclusively inside a fresh temporary directory: a sentinel under an existing `_staging/same-run/` was deleted; a second sentinel under a synthetic directory outside `results/` was also deleted. Normally generated IDs are safe; the defect concerns accepted caller-supplied/reused IDs and cleanup ownership.

**Acceptance:** validate run IDs as single safe path components and enforce resolved containment; clean up only a staging directory created and owned by the current invocation. Add collision, concurrent/reused-ID, traversal, absolute-path, and cleanup-ownership cases. Existing work must survive rejected publication.

### F2 — P1: Credential-style text can survive the redaction boundary

**Owner:** D; C tests each relevant output/diagnostic sink.

**Location:** `tradingagents/runapi/redact.py:7–12,17–25,40–41`.

The string filter does not redact an environment-style label with a provider prefix. The synthetic string `OPENAI_API_KEY=[REDACTED] is returned unchanged. The word boundary before `api_key` does not match after an underscore. Dictionary key filtering handles this case differently, but free text and exception diagnostics use the string path, which is also used for persisted reports/logs.

This demonstrates a bypass; it does not establish that a real credential has already leaked.

**Acceptance:** cover provider-prefixed labels, quoted/multiline credential assignments, authorization forms, and actual configured secret values using synthetic canaries. Verify persisted artifacts and diagnostics, not only dictionaries. Avoid recording real secrets in fixtures or evidence.

### F3 — P1: The semantic gate accepts a sparse, unrelated scoring sheet as PASS

**Owner:** C; E must not treat this scorer as a sufficient production gate yet.

**Locations:** `tests/member_c_verification/live/score_gov004.py:113–127,152–167,212–236`.

The scorer sums whatever answer rows are present. It does not verify that case/attempt IDs refer to the selected runs, that every applicable rubric item is present exactly once, or that critical items were evaluated. Artifact eligibility checks file existence without checking the manifest's identity or its correspondence to the report.

A synthetic fixture with ten mechanically eligible completed rows, placeholder reports, empty `{}` manifests, and **one score of 1 for an unrelated case/run** returned exit code 0 and `FINAL VERDICT: PASS`. The documented current rubric requires 28 applicable answers for the ten-run population. The existing exit-code tests check verdict-to-exit-code behavior; they do not establish completeness of the semantic assessment.

**Acceptance:** validate scoring and evidence schemas; bind scores to selected case/run/trial IDs; derive required rubric cells from a frozen applicability matrix; reject missing, duplicate, unknown, and inapplicably N/A cells. Verify manifest identity/configuration/revision and artifact correspondence. Add negative fixtures where these defects prevent PASS. Human judgment of narrative quality remains necessary.

### F4 — P2: Selecting only completed replacements hides failures from the completion denominator

**Owner:** C, with A confirming the formal population; D retains application-level accounting.

**Locations:** `tests/member_c_verification/live/score_gov004.py:130–148,193–221`; `docs/req/selected-requirements.md:116–120`.

The scorer selects the first two eligible **completed** attempts per case and compares the selected count with a constant ten. Failed starts appear in the printed history but cannot reduce the reported completion fraction when later attempts replace them.

A synthetic population of 20 started runs, ten incomplete and ten completed, still reported `completed runs: 10/10 ... PASS`. SEL-TA-NFR-006 requires all started fresh runs in the completion denominator, which would be 10/20 for that population.

**Acceptance:** report overall started/completed/review-needed/incomplete counts and the true completion fraction separately from semantic scores on completed reports. If the formal gate uses a particular ten-attempt cohort, freeze its membership before outcomes are known, retain its failed slots, and report retries separately. Reconcile that policy explicitly with NFR-006. This probe does not prove the documented latest ten-run live population contained failures; it exposes the scorer's behavior when failures occur.

### F5 — P2: The new layering tests pass after scanning zero source files

**Owner:** C.

**Locations:** `tests/member_c_verification/offline/test_nfr005_layering.py:19–25,45–66`.

`Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]` resolves to `<repo>/tests`, so both structural tests search non-existent `<repo>/tests/tradingagents/...` directories. The observed source-file count is **zero**. An empty offender list therefore does not demonstrate the required dependency direction or absence of terminal prompting in the engine layers.

**Acceptance:** discover the real repository root (currently `parents[3]` at this location), assert source directories exist and the scan is nonempty, and add a negative fixture proving a forbidden import fails. Cover actual prompt entry points used by this project, including `typer`/direct input as appropriate to the approved rule. Re-run the check before retaining its verification claim.

### F6 — P2: The interactive file picker hides portfolio-validation diagnostics

**Owner:** D; C covers the actual CLI interaction.

**Locations:** `cli/input_ui.py:62–72`; `tradingagents/runapi/result.py:20`.

`InputError` inherits from `ValueError`. `_choose_file()` catches `ValueError` before `InputError`, so a valid menu number selecting an invalid portfolio is treated as an invalid number. Its specific error detail and intended retry/cancel interaction are unreachable on that path. Tests of the input service alone do not cover this CLI behavior.

**Acceptance:** isolate number parsing from file loading or catch the more specific exception first. Test a valid selection of malformed JSON/invalid fields and verify an actionable file diagnostic and the intended retry/cancel flow, with no engine/provider call.

### F7 — P2: Recorded context-budget configuration is not applied at agent call sites

**Owner:** D; C adds behavioral coverage against a small configured cap.

**Locations:** `tradingagents/runapi/execution.py:82–83`; `tradingagents/default_config.py:126–127`; `tradingagents/agents/context.py:261–270`; agent call sites including `tradingagents/agents/analysts/turn.py:26–28` and `tradingagents/agents/researchers/bull_researcher.py:52`.

The effective configuration records `context_cap_tokens` and `compaction_threshold_tokens`, but the application call sites invoke `bound_agent_prompt(prompt)` with its defaults. Changing those configuration values changes the manifest without changing the guard's actual cap/threshold. This undermines reproducibility and enforcement of a configured budget.

**Acceptance:** pass the effective per-run budget through every applicable model invocation and test captured input size under non-default values. Ensure the manifest records the values actually enforced.

**Related design check:** string compaction preserves positional edges, not named protected fields. A synthetic constraint in a long prompt's middle was removed. This alone does not prove a production invariant is currently lost, but D/C should verify identity, consent/mode, provenance, and required policy constraints survive compaction in real assembled prompts or fail closed when protected content cannot fit.

### F8 — P2: Member C's original claimed formal live PASS cannot be independently audited from this checkout

**Owner:** C supplies sanitized evidence; E provides durable accessible retention; A confirms acceptance.

**Location:** `docs/verification/semantic-evaluation.md`, especially §§3,5,8–9.

The report claims 10/10 completed, 28/28 rubric passes, and 4/4 challenge exposures at source revision `git:e975528`. Its underlying evidence JSON, score file, reports, and manifests are described as gitignored and were absent from the initially updated checkout. Running the included scorer here finds zero evidence files and returns PENDING. The quoted observations in the Markdown report are useful but do not replace inspectable per-run artifacts and scores.

This is an evidence-availability limitation, not an allegation that the live runs did not happen. Live output is nondeterministic; rerunning a paid evaluation would not reconstruct the original evidence.

**Acceptance:** provide a sanitized, durable evidence package or accessible archive with relative paths, exact run IDs, source revision, configuration/prompt hashes, per-cell scoring/citations, challenge-exposure records, and integrity hashes. Make the scorer work against that package from a fresh checkout. Reconcile the scoring table's C2/C3 `t1/t3` labels with the stated trial-1/trial-2 population. Keep the system's `NEEDS_REVIEW` distinct from human semantic judgment, as the current report correctly does. A live result at an earlier revision also needs an explicit applicability assessment before claiming it covers the current head.

### F9 — P2: A live explicit-empty portfolio report gives instructions about existing exposure

**Owner:** D fixes prompt/context behavior; C owns semantic regression/evidence; A/B decide any change to the authoritative check contract.

**Evidence:** diagnostic C2 run `20261118T091902Z-08b8c0fa`, source `ee7a0a8` (review-document-only dirty marker), school `CS5351/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` via the saved `openai_compatible` configuration. Input is the existing fixed `GOV004-C2-explicit-empty` fixture, `PortfolioContext(positions=[])`, with no cash supplied. It is a known flat snapshot, not unknown holdings.

The run completed with final rating **Underweight** and deterministic check **PASSED**, but its Trader says: “reduce existing exposure to roughly 50–60% of a standard AAPL allocation.” The Portfolio Manager's Executive Summary says: “hold exposure at ~50–55% of target weight.” Neither passage conditions that instruction on an existing holding or acknowledges that the supplied portfolio has no AAPL position.

This is an observed ownership/context inconsistency against SEL-TA-FR-004/005 and the intended empty-versus-absent distinction. An Underweight research rating can be valid for a flat portfolio; an unconditional instruction to reduce/retain an existing position conflicts with that supplied state. It does not demonstrate an executed trade.

**Code investigation:** `tradingagents/portfolio.py:51–68` explicitly renders `No current position in AAPL`; the graph carries that rendering into state. `tradingagents/agents/managers/portfolio_manager.py:30–32` treats any supplied portfolio block as a current-position Hold context, while its rating legend at lines 54–59 unconditionally describes Underweight as reducing exposure/taking profits. These are plausible contributors, not a proven sole root cause. Inspect actual post-compaction prompts and upstream debate carryover. The deterministic Q1–Q4 checker is intentionally narrower than ownership semantics; its PASS does not override this finding. The live pytest itself only checks recorded-case count (`test_gov004_live.py:125–127`), so its success also cannot establish semantic acceptance.

**Acceptance:** preserve a five-tier research rating while making position-specific guidance conditional on actual supplied positions; for an explicit flat snapshot, avoid instructions to trim/retain a nonexistent holding. C should add independent positive/negative cases for no portfolio, flat portfolio, held target, another held ticker, and unknown cash; verify the context survives prompt assembly/compaction and adjudicate actual narratives. Do not claim an application-wide factual/ownership guarantee from a new keyword test. Any additional authoritative runtime check needs an agreed requirement/design change.

The reviewer paused further live cases when this defect was identified. An already-started C3 attempt was cooperatively interrupted and its incomplete record retained. Brian then explicitly authorized continuing the remaining diagnostics with F9 recorded; the new C3 attempt is counted separately rather than replacing the interrupted start.

## Other delivery and governance gaps

These are pending team work rather than newly attributed application regressions:

- **A/E — GOV-002:** `docs/req/selected-requirements.md` is present, but the final approved requirements registry and schema are not in the tracked delivery tree. The selected Markdown explicitly says it is not their substitute.

4. **B:** review any implementation-driven architecture deviations after D's changes; no architecture rewrite is required solely to acknowledge this review.

# Architecture Blueprint — Portfolio-Aware CLI and Auditable Reporting

Status: **architecture draft (Stage 3)** for Member B's session. Not implementation, not verification, not an approved course deliverable until E/team assembly and instructor reconciliation. Complements the D2 artifacts under `docs/architecture/`.

- Selection: **C2 — input-service + immutable `RunContext` boundary with a small lifecycle coordinator**, chosen by Brian (human) on 2026-11-12 based on **estimated** tradeoffs, not verified superiority.
- Target baseline: TradingAgents **v0.7.1** (`tradingagents/__init__.py:3`, `pyproject.toml`).
- Working scope: `docs/req/selected-requirements.md` (`SEL-TA-FR-001..007`, `SEL-TA-NFR-001..006`, `SEL-TA-GOV-001..006`). This is a working selection, **not** an approved D1 registry.
- Location convention (interim, pending course clarification): this root file is canonical; `docs/architecture/architecture-blueprint.md` is a pointer only.

> Honesty statement: This document specifies architecture and testability. It does **not** claim C's tests exist/pass, E's gates are enforced, or any approval has been obtained. Unknown test IDs and implementation links remain **pending**. Estimates are labelled **ESTIMATE**.

---

## 1. Scope and drivers

### 1.1 Scope
Extend the existing terminal UI (`cli/`), the Python/LangGraph workflow (`tradingagents/`), the portfolio loader (`tradingagents/portfolio.py`) and the Markdown/HTML reports (`tradingagents/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/report_html.py`) so a run can be performed in one of two input modes:

- `NO_PORTFOLIO` — the caller's holdings/cash are unknown; nothing is assumed.
- `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED` — an explicitly selected, validated, frozen snapshot supplied by the user.

Both modes yield an auditable result with deterministic input provenance and a deterministic output check.

### 1.2 Drivers
| Driver | Source |
|---|---|
| Optional, explicitly confirmed holdings input | selected-requirements §1; Brian decision |
| No silent portfolio fallback; no invented zero holdings/cash | FR-003/004, NFR-001 |
| Deterministic check authority (model cannot override) | FR-007 |
| Frozen input provenance in every report | FR-006 |
| Secret/holdings privacy across sinks | NFR-003 |
| Reusable boundary without terminal prompts in engine/agents | NFR-005 |
| Reliable external-failure handling | NFR-001 |
| Structured observability | NFR-002 |
| Cohesive integration preserving upstream | NFR-005 |

### 1.3 Explicit non-goals (deferred; do not claim satisfied)
Web GUI; broker connection/order execution; exposure certification; automatic broker discovery; full twelve-channel evidence registry; new historical filtering/freshness rules; global source-confidence grades; R4–R6 sentiment correction; resume/checkpoint redesign; aggregate time/token/call budgets; debate convergence; analyst plugin redesign. (selected-requirements §5.)

### 1.4 Authority of current selection vs open decisions
- **Approved working input (use directly):** CLI-only UI; `PORTFOLIO_DIR=<project-root>/portfolios`; `--without-portfolio`; `--portfolio-as-of`; consent behaviour; full normalized-content SHA-256 (64-char) fingerprint.
- **Open (not B's to close; do not invent):** final D1 YAML/schema approval (A); semantic rubric/threshold (`GOV-004`, C/A); instructor-accepted source/test layout and transcript wording; governance install (E); blueprint location final convention (E).

---

## 2. System and deployment boundaries

- **Runtime:** a single local Python process. The user interacts through the terminal (the existing CLI). No network is required for input selection/validation; network/provider calls occur only inside the graph after confirmation.
- **Requested interface:** current CLI (`cli/main.py`), extended with input-mode flags. This is the only new user-facing surface; no new web application.
- **Baseline preserved:** `tradingagents/`, `cli/`, `pyproject.toml` and existing tests are preserved. The extension is discovery, explicit consent, frozen provenance and coherent reporting (Prompt.md "Session objective and input precedence" / "Access and output boundaries").
- **Trust boundary for data:** user-supplied portfolio files are *context*, never verified account facts. The trusted state used to build provenance is the frozen snapshot produced by the input service, not model text and not re-read file bytes.

### 2.1 Data-flow (C2)

## 1. Scope and drivers

### 1.1 Scope
Extend the existing terminal UI (`cli/`), the Python/LangGraph workflow (`tradingagents/`), the portfolio loader (`tradingagents/portfolio.py`) and the Markdown/HTML reports (`tradingagents/reporting.py`, `tradingagents/report_html.py`) so a run can be performed in one of two input modes:

- `NO_PORTFOLIO` — the caller's holdings/cash are unknown; nothing is assumed.
- `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED` — an explicitly selected, validated, frozen snapshot supplied by the user.

Both modes yield an auditable result with deterministic input provenance and a deterministic output check.

### 1.2 Drivers
| Driver | Source |
|---|---|
| Optional, explicitly confirmed holdings input | selected-requirements §1; Brian decision |
| No silent portfolio fallback; no invented zero holdings/cash | FR-003/004, NFR-001 |
| Deterministic check authority (model cannot override) | FR-007 |
| Frozen input provenance in every report | FR-006 |
| Secret/holdings privacy across sinks | NFR-003 |
| Reusable boundary without terminal prompts in engine/agents | NFR-005 |
| Reliable external-failure handling | NFR-001 |
| Structured observability | NFR-002 |
| Cohesive integration preserving upstream | NFR-005 |

### 1.3 Explicit non-goals (deferred; do not claim satisfied)
Web GUI; broker connection/order execution; exposure certification; automatic broker discovery; full twelve-channel evidence registry; new historical filtering/freshness rules; global source-confidence grades; R4–R6 sentiment correction; resume/checkpoint redesign; aggregate time/token/call budgets; debate convergence; analyst plugin redesign. - **Runtime:** a single local Python process. The user interacts through the terminal (the existing CLI). No network is required for input selection/validation; network/provider calls occur only inside the graph after confirmation.

# CS5351 Architecture Session Handoff — Member B

Capture time: 2026-11-20 15:16 HKT (+0800) / 2026-11-20T07:16Z. Author: the OpenCode assistant acting as Member B's architecture session. This is a **summary handoff**, not a verbatim transcript or proof that any course deliverable is complete.

## Summary

This session was Member B's architecture session for the CS5351 extension of TradingAgents v0.7.1: a portfolio-aware CLI with auditable reporting. It produced (as **drafts**) a chosen architecture (C2), contracts, invariants, state/memory design, permission model, runtime policy catalog, evaluation table, and traceability inputs. All architecture documents are **proposed drafts pending A's final requirements, C's independent tests and E's governance/assembly**; they are not approved implementation requirements. Application code, tests, requirements, governance and review files were **not** modified in this handoff task, and this handoff intentionally does not comment on the current status of E's ongoing fix work.

Source-tracking classification used below:
- **[Course obligation]** — required by the brief, not optional.
- **[Recorded decision]** — a decision or approval actually made by a human/team in this session or repository (attributable; not invented).
- **[Proposed/pending]** — a design proposal or decision awaiting the named owner/course confirmation.
- **[Historical claim]** — a statement carried in review/evidence documents; not independently re-verified by this handoff as current code truth.
- **[Repo fact]** — verified from the current repository during this handoff.

---

## A. Project and role

- **[Repo fact]** Project: TradingAgents v0.7.1 enhancement for CS5351 (course-extension of an upstream open-source multi-agent trading framework).
- **[Course obligation]** My role is **Member B: architecture, contracts, invariants, state, and authority/permission design.** B does not approve A's requirements, does not author C's verification conclusions, and does not implement application code for D.

## A. Project and role

- **[Course obligation]** My role is **Member B: architecture, contracts, invariants, state, and authority/permission design.** B does not approve A's requirements, does not author C's verification conclusions, and does not implement application code for D.
- **[Recorded decision / ownership]** Accountable owners (from the team allocation document): **A** owns final requirements/registry; **C** owns independent verification and test code; **D** owns application code; **E** owns governance/CI, shared traceability assembly and packaging; **B** owns architecture artifacts. Implementation changes must follow the team's supervised OpenCode process with C's approved tests and E's gates.
- **[Historical claim]** E is currently investigating fixes (per the 2026-11-18 project review, D's fixes F1/F2 then F6/F7 are recommended first). **This handoff does not assert the current status of E's or D's work.** Do not invent it.

---

## B. Architecture continuity

### Selected design (must be preserved)
- **[Recorded decision]** **C2 — input-service + immutable `RunContext` boundary with a small CLI lifecycle coordinator** (plus a shared, prompt-free execution service). Chosen by Brian (human) on 2026-11-12 on the basis of **estimated** tradeoffs, explicitly **not** verified superiority. C1 (minimal inline) and C3 (phased façade) were genuine alternatives, documented but rejected.
- Rejected/deferred options (must remain documented, not re-run): C1, C3, inline-only validation, newest/first-file default, treating absent as flat / zero-cash, persisting full payload, truncated-12 fingerprint for new provenance, web GUI/broker/order execution, resume/checkpoint redesign, aggregate run budgets, global source-confidence and sentiment correction. See `docs/architecture/option-ledger.md` and `option-ledger.md`.

### Key contracts (summary; authoritative text in files)
- **Input modes:** `NO_PORTFOLIO` (unknown) vs `PORTFOLIO_PROVIDED` (explicit frozen snapshot).
- **Consent:** a frozen snapshot is **not** a confirmed selection; only an explicit `CONFIRMED` transition authorizes execution. Interactive prompts only in the CLI; non-interactive uses `--portfolio PATH (+ --portfolio-as-of)` or `--without-portfolio`.
- **Provenance:** full 64-char SHA-256 over a **canonical JSON byte string**; total position ordering (null-price handling, broker-alias ties), deep-immutable value tuples; upstream 12-char checkpoint fingerprint preserved separately.
- **Check authority:** deterministic `OutputChecker` (Q1 rating readable; Q2 header identity vs **explicit trusted metadata**; Q3 disclaimer present; Q4 prohibited phrases absent). One authoritative call on the **completed** path; incomplete runs **bypass** the checker and get `NOT_RUN`. `OUTPUT CHECK: PASSED` text from the model cannot override. Q1–Q4 do **not** certify narrative semantics.
- **Publication:** report+manifest are **critical** and published by a **single atomic directory commit**; the JSONL terminal event is **best-effort** (on append failure the logical outcome is preserved and `terminal_event.durable=false`). Empty-findings equivalence is qualified to completed runs.
- **API boundary:** supported project API routes through the shared execution service (full coverage); the raw `TradingAgentsGraph` primitive is a declared reduced-coverage compatibility path whose product reliance requires **A's approval** (open).

### Canonical document locations and reading order
Root blueprint is canonical; `docs/architecture/architecture-blueprint.md` is a pointer only.
1. `architecture-blueprint.md` (canonical blueprint)
2. `docs/architecture/adr/001-portfolio-aware-cli.md` (decision + layered context + budget)
3. `docs/architecture/interface-contracts.md` (types, canonicalization, schemas, state machine, check/publication ordering)
4. `docs/architecture/invariants.md` (INV-01..14/05b with fallbacks)
5. `docs/architecture/memory-design.md` (state/privacy/retention/sinks)
6. `docs/architecture/runtime-policy-catalog.md` (failure/degraded paths)
7. `docs/architecture/permission-model.md` (A/B/C/D/E roles)
8. `docs/architecture/evaluation-table.md` (candidate comparison, weights, sensitivity)
9. `docs/architecture/risk-list.md`, `option-ledger.md`, `evaluation-logbook.md` (supporting)
10. `docs/architecture/traceability-inputs-member-b.md` (B's rows for E's matrix; test IDs/impl links pending)

### Decisions to preserve and genuine unresolved issues
- **[Recorded decision]** The fixed working inputs: CLI-only UI; `PORTFOLIO_DIR=<root>/portfolios`; `--without-portfolio`; `--portfolio-as-of D`; full normalized-content SHA-256; consent behaviour. Do not reopen these absent a direct contradiction.
- **[Proposed/pending]** Final D1 registry/schema (A); semantic rubric/threshold and test approval (C/A); governance install and CI gates (E); instructor layout/transcript interpretation (E); A's approval of any product reliance on the reduced-coverage raw primitive; canonicalization must be implemented exactly (D).

### Constraints on this handoff
- **No new candidate evaluation or architecture redesign** is performed here. This file records continuity only.

---

## C. Current requirements clarification (preserve these intentions)

These are the intended semantics carried from this session's requirements work; the **next session should examine whether FR-004/FR-005 need clearer generated-report acceptance criteria**. It must **not** silently add a new authoritative check or rewrite A's final requirements.

- **[Recorded/intended]** Users may confirm and proceed **without** a portfolio.
- `NO_PORTFOLIO` means **unknown** holdings (not flat).
- An **explicit empty positions list** means a supplied **flat** snapshot.
- A supplied portfolio **can contain other instruments while having no position in the analyzed instrument** (that target simply has no current position).
- **Missing cash is unknown, not zero.**
- **Empty holdings do not require rejecting the run or forcing Hold** — a valid research rating (including Underweight/Sell) is allowed for a flat book.
- **Research ratings are distinct from account-specific instructions.** Portfolio context must not convert a research rating into an executable account instruction; position-specific guidance should be conditional on actual supplied positions.
- **Current PASSED checks Q1–Q4 only** and does **not** certify all narrative semantics.

This is exactly the tension behind F9 (below): the check PASSED while the narrative addressed existing exposure that was not supplied.

---

## D. Evidence and next-session reading (read-only; verified in this handoff)

Target checkout: `/home/brian/projects/CS5351`.
- **[Repo fact]** Branch `main`, HEAD commit `e7aed7a9d735c7524eca583be1c2ed569f8c5ac2` ("docs: record Member B review and live diagnostic evidence", 2026-11-18 18:03 +0800). Working tree clean at capture (`git status --porcelain` empty). Do not pull/switch/alter the target checkout.
- Note: the review record describes the application revision under test as `ee7a0a8e…` / `git:ee7a0a8+dirty` (integration commit merging C's PR #3). The current HEAD `e7aed7a` is a later docs commit on `main`. If exact applicability matters, compare `e7aed7a` against `ee7a0a8` rather than assuming identity.

Files inspected read-only this handoff (all present):
- `docs/req/selected-requirements.md` — confirms two modes, empty-is-flat, other-instruments-allowed, missing-cash-not-zero, no-portfolio notice, Q1–Q4 limited checks, FR-004/005 wording.
- `docs/reviews/project-review-2026-11-18.md` — F1–F9 findings, live diagnostic table, delivery/governance gaps.
- `docs/reviews/evidence/live-diagnostic-2026-11-18.json` — 6 started / 5 completed diagnostic records; `formal_gate_pass: false`.
- `architecture-blueprint.md` — the same C2 draft blueprint produced by this session.

### F9 explained accurately
- **[Historical claim, per review + evidence]** The `GOV004-C2-explicit-empty` run (`20261118T091902Z-08b8c0fa`) used the fixed explicit-empty fixture `PortfolioContext(positions=[])` with **no cash supplied** — a known **flat** snapshot, not unknown holdings. It **completed**, final rating **Underweight**, deterministic check **PASSED**. But its Trader/Portfolio Manager narrative referred to **reducing/retaining existing exposure** (e.g., "reduce existing exposure to roughly 50–60%…", "hold exposure at ~50–55% of target weight") without conditioning on the supplied flat holdings.
- **The concern is the wording**, i.e. an ownership/context inconsistency against FR-004/FR-005. It is **not** a defect of the optional-portfolio feature, not a rejection of explicit-empty runs, and **not** caused by the mere presence of `PASSED` (Q1–Q4 are intentionally narrower than ownership semantics).
